title: Chunk reorder + pause/resume repro & debug playbook
body:
SUMMARY:
This is a personal playbook for reproducing and debugging an intermittent streaming issue we've seen in a subset of hosted requests: when a client pauses reading (e.g. slow consumer / backpressure), the server sometimes emits chunk fragments that later arrive out of order or are replayed after resume.

Symptoms observed (high level):
- Clients see duplicate partial frames or re-ordered chunks after a deliberate read-pause > ~150ms.
- Some clients report "partial JSON" frames followed by the remainder later, but occasionally a small token chunk appears before an earlier chunk (reordering).
- Issue surface: affects SSE/text-stream endpoints (responses/stream) with long outputs (>2s of token streaming) under moderate concurrency.
- Not always correlated with error logs on server; sometimes only client-visible artifacts.

Quick reproduction intent:
- Create a small client that connects to streaming endpoint, reads n chunks, pauses (sleep) on the socket, then resumes; observe order & duplicates.
- Vary pause duration and concurrency to map threshold.

ENV used for repro (my laptop to cluster):
- macOS 13.6 -> local node repro client
- Cluster serving-runtime branch: mainish + PR 2148 (experimental flush changes)
- Model: gpt-small-ish (deterministic prompt)
- Endpoint: POST https://api.redwood-internal/v1/responses/stream (internal staging)

REPRO STEPS (simple curl-ish):
1) naive SSE using curl (control test):
   curl -N -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n     -X POST https://api.redwood-internal/v1/responses/stream \n     -d '{"input":"repeat: token i 0..100","stream":true}' > /tmp/out1.txt
   Inspect out1.txt for ordering issues. (curl -N is not great for pausing mid-stream)

2) node test that pauses/resumes mid-stream (recommended):
   // run: node pause-resume-client.js
   const https = require('https');
   const opts = {
     hostname: 'api.redwood-internal',
     path: '/v1/responses/stream',
     method: 'POST',
     headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + process.env.TEST, 'Accept': 'text/event-stream', 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }
   };
   const req = https.request(opts, (res) => {
     res.setEncoding('utf8');
     let buf = '';
     res.on('data', (chunk) => {
       const ts = Date.now();
       console.log(`DATA ${ts} LEN=${chunk.length} --->`, JSON.stringify(chunk.slice(0,80)));
       buf += chunk;
       // pause consumer after first N bytes
       if (buf.length > 120 && !globalPaused) {
         globalPaused = true;
         console.log('pausing read for 250ms');
         res.pause();
         setTimeout(() => { console.log('resuming'); res.resume(); }, 250);
       }
     });
     res.on('end', () => { console.log('END'); });
   });
   req.write(JSON.stringify({input: 'tokenized test 0..250', stream: true }));
   req.end();

3) python/eventsource client (alternative):
   from sseclient import SSEClient
   import requests
   r = requests.post(url, headers=hdrs, json=payload, stream=True)
   client = SSEClient(r)
   i=0
   for event in client.events():
       print('EV', i, event.data[:80])
       i+=1
       if i==3:
           time.sleep(0.35)  # pause consumer

Observed failures during local runs:
- Example run (node): logs show chunk sizes and times:
  DATA 1700 LEN=64 ---> "":token: hello\n"
  DATA 1701 LEN=18 ---> "\n\n"
  pausing read for 250ms
  resuming
  DATA 1958 LEN=48 ---> "":token: world\n"
  DATA 1959 LEN=64 ---> "":token: hello\n"  <-- duplicate of earlier 'hello' after resume

- Sometimes the 'hello' reappears interleaved between later tokens (reorder), not always an exact duplicate (partial suffix/prefix).

Server-side snippets (what I looked at):
- No obvious 5xx logs for these requests.
- Access logs show single connection, 200 response, streaming; chunk sizes logged at various flush points.
- Runtime has two relevant code paths: earlyFlush (after first token) and periodicFlush (every 20ms batch). PR 2148 tweaks flushing heuristics.

Commands tried and quick results:
- tcpdump on node nic while reproducing: tcpdump -w out.pcap port 443 and inspect with tshark -> saw packets buffered and retransmitted after pause, but ordering in pcap looks sequential at TCP level (no reordering in TCP).
- strace (on staging proxy): not available (prod), but on local server binary I ran strace and saw write() syscalls spaced, no duplicate writes at the app libc layer.
- curl --no-buffer vs --buffer: toggling didn't change outcome consistently.
- Disabled keepalive on client (socket.setKeepAlive(false)) reduced frequency of repros but didn't eliminate.
- Lowered TCP_NODELAY (enabled) -> toggling Nagle didn't fix.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Client read pause causes libuv/Node to coalesce buffered chunks when resume happens, emitting in slightly different groupings; downstream event parsing then interprets boundaries differently leading to duplicate/partial parse artifacts. (Client-side parser state may be brittle).
2) Server flush logic sometimes duplicates a tail fragment when switching between streaming paths (earlyFlush + periodicFlush race) — e.g., same token appended to two different flush buffers due to a small race. (App-level duplication)
3) Proxy (nginx/envoy) buffering + flow-control interactions cause chunk re-injection or delay that the client mis-parses as duplicate.
4) TLS library internal buffering in the server/proxy combined with connection 'pause' at TCP level leads to reassembly differences in user-space—rare but plausible with partial writes.

Tests to discriminate quickly:
- Client-only elimination test: use a minimal blocking client (Python socket recv with exact byte reads) to ensure parser maintains state; if issue goes away -> client parser is fragile.
- Server echo test: run a tiny local server that streams numbered tokens with same flush behavior; run our client against it. If repro occurs locally with local server, then server flush/OS stack rather than remote proxy is implicated.
- Proxy bypass: use curl to target the service on the nodeport/pod IP (bypass gateway) to see if proxy contributes.

Experiment logs (short):
- Local micro-server (Go) that writes "TOKEN i\n" every 20ms, and on a pause on client, I did not see duplicates. That points away from pure OS/TCP-level reordering.
- Running the real staging server binary locally and pausing the client reproduced the duplication once in ~20 runs. On the same binary, instrumenting flush() callsite and dumping buffers before/after flush showed a duplicated slice in the ring buffer once. -> points to server-level race in buffer ownership.

Things to inspect in runtime code (notes for devs):
- streaming_writer.go / writer.go: look for where a token is appended to both pending_flush and immediate_flush lists. Race between goroutine A (token append) and goroutine B (flush snapshot) could record same pointer twice. Use a copy-on-append or mark-as-owned semantics.
- periodic flusher: ensure it clears the pending buffer atomically AFTER snapshotting.
- earlyFlush path (on first token): ensure it consumes/clears the pending buffer rather than duplicating.

Suggested quick fixes to test in canary (small, easy-to-revert):
- Add per-request atomic write mutex around flush snapshot and append operations.
- Add a sequence number per chunk emitted from server, log it, and verify dedupe on client. (Helps triage in production).
- Extra diagnostics: on each flush, write an opaque flush-id and chunk-offset into logs; correlate with client-observed duplicates.

Notes on client parsing fragility (if relevant):
- Our client code assumes that each SSE event contains a full JSON object per data: line. If server splits a JSON across two writes and those get coalesced differently after pause/resume, our parser may reassemble wrong. Robust approach: stream-parse by braces and not by event boundaries.

Next steps (short actionable list):
- [ ] Run local instrumented staging binary with atomic counters and enable per-chunk metadata for 1% of production requests (via feature flag).
- [ ] Add unit test that exercises quick pause/resume in the existing flusher test suite (simulate append+flush race).
- [ ] If server-level race is confirmed, land small mutex around append/flush (temporary) and run soak.
- [ ] If only client parser fails, harden client parsing and add tests.

Notes / misc debug crumbs: 
- best repro pause window: 120ms-600ms; above 1s usually drains fully and less likely to show reorder.
- more likely to repro under moderate concurrency (40-120 concurrent streams) than single-client.
- seen more often in region eu-west-1 cluster nodes on t4g-ish instances (maybe perf related).

TL;DR: start by reproducing locally with instrumented server binary (dump append/flush buffer contents), then add lightweight sequence numbers on chunks and short-term mutex around flush path. If that reproduces fix -> roll to canary. If not, revert and continue isolating between proxy/TLS/client parsing.

Owner / follow-up: Evelyn (me) will run the instrumented binary experiments this week (blocking steps: need debug build from infra and a short canary channel). Ping @Ravi for help adding small flush-id instrumentation and @Marta for client parsing review.

RAW LOG SNIPPET (example):
[2026-02-25T17:01:12.124Z] flush-id=314 token_count=1 bufLen=64 -> "{"type":"delta","chunk":"hello"}"
[2026-02-25T17:01:12.149Z] client paused (res.pause)
[2026-02-25T17:01:12.378Z] flush-id=315 token_count=2 bufLen=112 -> "{"type":"delta","chunk":"world"}"
[2026-02-25T17:01:12.383Z] flush-id=316 token_count=1 bufLen=64 -> "{"type":"delta","chunk":"hello"}"  <-- duplicated text

(reasonable suspicion: race that copies same chunk into two consecutive flush snapshots)

END OF NOTE - keep as private scratchpad.
